subject: Messaging review: onboarding sequence (email + console nudges + landing pages)
body:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, Jan 18, 2026 at 9:12 AM PST
Subject: Messaging review: onboarding sequence (email + console nudges + landing pages)

Ben — did a pass on the email v2 + the current console nudge drafts + the landing page snippets linked from the CTAs.

High-level feedback:
1) We’re slightly inconsistent on the “why Redwood” value prop. Some touchpoints lead with cost, others with latency, others with reliability. We can mix, but the first touch in each channel should anchor on the same promise.
2) CTA verbs differ across surfaces ("Get API key" vs "Create an API key" vs "Generate key"). Recommend we standardize to one.
3) We should be careful with superlatives (e.g., “fastest inference”) unless we can cite it. Safer: “low-latency, production-grade inference” + “predictable performance”.

Proposed positioning line (consistent across email header + first console nudge + landing hero):
- "Ship LLM features with low-latency, reliable inference—without running GPUs."

Suggested CTA standard:
- Primary: "Create API key"
- Secondary: "Run your first request"

Copy edits (most important):

A) Email 1 (signup)
Current subject options include “Your API key is ready” — but key is not ready until they create it. Recommend:
- Subject: "Create your Redwood API key (2 min)"
- Preheader: "Run your first request and start measuring latency + cost."

Body opening (suggested):
“Welcome to Redwood Inference. Create an API key and run your first request in minutes. Once you’re live, the Console will show token-level latency and cost so you can tune for production.”

Avoid: “Start for free with 100k tokens” in the very first line. It’s okay to mention credits, but leading with it attracts deal-seekers and can undercut the production/performance story.

B) Console nudge: API key creation
Replace “Generate key” with “Create API key”. Also recommend making the nudge outcome-oriented:
- Title: “Create an API key”
- Body: “You’ll use this key for your first request. You can rotate keys anytime.”
- CTA: “Create API key”
- Secondary link: “See quickstart”

C) Console nudge: First request
If we mention streaming, let’s avoid implying it’s required. Suggest:
- Title: “Run your first request”
- Body: “Copy/paste a minimal snippet to get your first tokens back. Optional: enable streaming for faster perceived latency.”
- CTA: “Open quickstart”

D) Landing page snippet (docs PR / quickstart)
Where we currently say “Get started instantly,” swap to “Get started in ~5 minutes” only if true for a new account + no hidden steps. Otherwise:
- “Get started in minutes”

Also: ensure the landing page headline matches the email promise. If email says “low-latency, reliable inference,” landing should not lead with “cheapest tokens.” We can include cost right after.

If helpful I can mark these directly in the copy doc, but wanted to send the alignment notes first.

Soojin

—
Soojin Lee
Lifecycle Messaging (GTM)
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Messaging review: onboarding sequence (email + console nudges + landing pages)

This is super helpful — thank you.

Agree on standardizing CTAs. We’ve got “Get API key” currently because it was shorter in the nudge component, but I can push for “Create API key” everywhere.

Two questions:
1) For Email 2 (no API key after 24h): do we lead with reliability or keep it purely instructional? (We were going to make it “you’re one step away”.)
2) Do you have preferred phrasing for “Hosted API” vs just “Redwood API”? We’ve used both.

Also: are you ok with “Run your first request in under 5 minutes” if we qualify it as “most developers”? We don’t have a benchmark yet.

Ben


On Sun, Jan 18, 2026 at 10:02 AM Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, Jan 18, 2026 at 10:02 AM PST
Subject: Re: Messaging review: onboarding sequence (email + console nudges + landing pages)

1) Email 2 (no key @ 24h): I’d keep it primarily instructional, but put one sentence that reinforces the “why” (latency/reliability/visibility) so it doesn’t feel like nagging.

Suggested structure:
- Subject: “Still need an API key?” (or “Create your API key to run a first request”)
- 2-line body: remind value + confirm it’s one step
- Big CTA: “Create API key”
- Tiny secondary: “Having trouble? Reply to this email” (reduces silent churn, and helps Support triage)

Example paragraph:
“Create an API key to run your first request and start tracking token-level latency and cost in the Console. It’s the quickest path to production-ready performance.”

2) Naming: I recommend “Redwood API” in emails/nudges (less jargon), and “Hosted API” can show up in product docs / pricing pages. In the onboarding flow, “Redwood API” is clearer.

3) On “under 5 minutes”: I’d avoid “under” / “most developers” unless we can back it up (we’ll get questioned). Safer:
- “in minutes”
- or “a minimal first request in minutes”

If we want specificity without the claim:
- “Typically: create key → paste snippet → see tokens.”

Also note: we should ensure the landing page + quickstart match the exact CTA labels, otherwise it feels broken.

Soojin

Subject: Re: Messaging review: onboarding sequence (email + console nudges + landing pages)

+1 on CTA standardization.

UX note: the nudge component has 22 chars before truncation in the button on smaller widths. “Create API key” fits, “Create an API key” wraps.

Proposed button labels:
- Button: “Create API key”
- Title can be “Create an API key” (longer is ok)

For “Run your first request” nudge, we can do:
- Button: “Open quickstart”

Also: we just added the email preferences entry point in console settings (PR is in review). Should we mention “Manage email preferences” anywhere in the onboarding sequence footer, or keep it only in unsubscribe?

Marissa

Subject: Re: Messaging review: onboarding sequence (email + console nudges + landing pages)

Love the 22-char constraint callout — thanks.

Re: preferences link: include it in the footer with unsubscribe, but don’t add additional emphasis in the email body.

Suggested footer language (consistent across all onboarding sends):
“You’re receiving this because you created a Redwood Inference account. Unsubscribe or manage email preferences.”

On the console side, it’s fine to leave preferences under Settings and not put it in a nudge (nudges should stay focused on “next best action”).

One more consistency note I missed: if emails say “Console” (capital C), console UI should match, and landing pages should do the same.

Soojin

Subject: Re: Messaging review: onboarding sequence (email + console nudges + landing pages)

Thanks all — this is the right level of rigor.

Decision / direction so we can move:
- Anchor promise: “low-latency + reliable inference” as primary. Cost comes immediately after, but not as the headline.
- Standardize CTAs: “Create API key” and “Open quickstart” (per Marissa’s constraint).
- Remove any “fastest/cheapest” language until we have benchmark substantiation.
- Add “manage email preferences” in footer across the series.

Ben — please incorporate in the v2 copy doc and flag any lines you feel are at risk of impacting CTR so we can A/B. Marissa — ship the console text with these labels.

Camila

—
Camila Reyes
VP, Growth
Redwood Inference
